claims.statement: Sustained/vigilant attention is a time-extended control problem distinct from initial capture, and performance commonly declines with increasing time on task.
Expected information gain and the subjective value of information are separable but interacting drivers of curiosity-guided exploration.
Learning progress and successful acquisition of information can reinforce curiosity for related information, supporting a dynamic rather than static curiosity model.
Goal congruence, certainty, control/coping potential, and agency/responsibility are empirically distinguishable appraisal dimensions with differentiated relationships to emotion states.
Appraisal-emotion mapping is many-to-many: a single appraisal dimension does not uniquely identify an emotion, and emotion categories do not arise from one appraisal alone.
Salient group identity can make group norms a basis for social influence, with effects moderated by identification and context.
Perceived group prototypicality is a distinct identity-relevant representation that can shape influence and collective behavior rather than being reducible to simple similarity.
Perceived authenticity/genuineness is a recurring, empirically measured influencer construct related to credibility outcomes but is not identical to trustworthiness, expertise, or objective truth.
Strategic displays of authenticity can backfire and recent synthesis does not support treating perceived authenticity as a universal engagement booster.
Modern online PSR measurement supports multidimensional representation including intimacy, relationship maintenance, and real-life relationship intention rather than a single closeness score.
Parasocial intimacy is a dimension of an enduring one-sided relationship and must not be inferred from mere repeated exposure/familiarity.
Perceived usefulness/information value can motivate interpersonal transmission, but the motive is distinct from the observed act of sharing.
Anticipated privacy costs can inhibit or reshape social-media disclosure/transmission decisions and must be modeled alongside expected gratifications.
Reputational and self-presentation concerns can alter what people transmit to an audience, especially under multiple-audience and feedback conditions.
Goal-directed control relies on action-outcome/world-model representations and current outcome values, whereas habitual/model-free strategies provide a partly distinct control route.

A separate arbitration mechanism is one supported account of habit-goal control, but alternative models integrate habit and goal influences without a discrete central arbiter; arbitration should therefore remain provisional rather than ontologically mandatory.
Outcome-devaluation insensitivity can be misclassified when the devaluation manipulation itself is ineffective, so apparent habit-like responding requires manipulation-validity checks.
